idiom_name: generator function with yield / yield from; generator expressions
implementation_notes: Any def containing yield is a generator function (PEP 255): calling it returns a generator object that suspends at each yield with the whole frame preserved - locals, statement position, exception state - and next()/for/comprehensions pull elements one at a time; yield from (PEP 380) delegates to a sub-iterable, and generator expressions give the same laziness without a named function. The frame is closed deterministically on .close() or when the object is collected, running finally blocks; itertools supplies the lazy adapters (islice, takewhile, chain, groupby) so the producing routine can stay small.
pitfalls: StopIteration must not escape a generator body: a bare next() that raises it inside the generator is converted to RuntimeError by PEP 479, so guard with next(it, None) or iterate instead of peeking.

Nothing runs until the first next(): setup errors (file open, parameter validation) surface at the consumer, and closing an abandoned generator raises GeneratorExit inside the frame, where swallowing it or yielding again is an error.

Generators are single-use, so an API that accepts one cannot iterate it twice: document the contract, prefer returning a fresh generator per call, and never share one generator between threads or tasks without external locking.

variants.name: Async generators (PEP 525)
variants.idiom_name: async def generator with yield, driven by async for and closed with aclose()
variants.implementation_notes: An async generator (PEP 525) is declared async def with yield: it may await inside the body and is consumed with async for or anext(); aclose() (and the event loop's finalisation hooks) run the frame's async cleanup, and task cancellation propagates into the suspended frame. Use it when element production awaits I/O - streaming responses, queue reads, socket frames - so that the consumer applies backpressure by awaiting each pull; keep the synchronous generator when nothing is awaited.
variants.code_sketch:
async def tail_log(path):
    async with aiofiles.open(path) as f:   # async I/O per element
        async for line in f:
            yield line.rstrip("\n")        # one line per pull

async for line in tail_log("app.log"):
    if "ERROR" in line:
        break          # aclose() runs the async cleanup path
pitfalls: Async generators are finalised through the event loop: relying on garbage collection to close one (no async with/aclosing) leaves the underlying socket or task pending and emits warnings, and the cleanup only runs if the loop is still alive.
A single async generator cannot be consumed by two tasks concurrently - interleaved anext() calls steal elements - so shared streams need an explicit queue or a single consumer task.
